extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting manuscripts (articles, proceedings, monographs) to AMS journals and book series (mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission rules and style/production requirements for manuscripts, graphics, and source files to the American Mathematical Society for journals, proceedings, and monographs. Covers LaTeX/AMS-TEX usage, graphics and image requirements, submission procedures, and front-matter/top-matter rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule line weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'hairline' weight; this will be nearly invisible at high resolution and will disappear in the printing process. If a rule line is gray or colored, its weight should be no thinner than 1 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use very thin (hairline) rules. Ensure gray/colored rules are >= 1 pt so they reproduce in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded line-weight increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Graded line weights should increase in increments of at least 0.5pt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increments less than 0.5pt are insufficiently distinguishable at high resolution; choose line-weight steps >= 0.5pt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screened fill percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened fills should be screened not less than 15% and not greater than 85%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less than 15% will print as white; greater than 85% will print as black. Keep screened fills within [15%,85%].

rubrics_metrics.name: Text in graphics: outlines vs bitmaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideally, text included in graphics files should be font outlines rather than bitmaps, because the AMS typesets on a high-resolution image-setter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If text in graphics is bitmapped at 300 dpi or less it may appear poor next to high-resolution text. Prefer outlined fonts; if bitmapped characters are part of bitmapped line art, aim for bitmapped characters at 1200 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bitmap resolution guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitmaps of characters at 300 dpi or less may appear poor; if bitmapped characters are part of line art, output will be ideal if the bitmapped characters are at 1200 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bitmap images containing text/characters use very high DPI (1200 dpi for bitmapped characters) to match AMS production quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonelectronic graphics drawing and paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonelectronic graphics should be drawn in black ink with clean, unbroken lines on nonabsorbent paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce crisp black-ink art on nonabsorbent paper; avoid absorbent surfaces that cause feathering or broken lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts in graphics should match text
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever possible, fonts used in graphics should match those used in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same fonts for labels and annotations in figures as in the main document to ensure visual consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' original graphics use
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors’ original graphics are used whenever possible in AMS publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send original artwork rather than photocopies when possible so production can use highest-quality source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photograph handling and packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the originals of photographs or electronic artwork; a photocopy can be used only to identify it. To avoid damage do not use paper clips/staples/tape; use cardboard backing and do not fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Package photographs carefully (cardboard backing, no staples/paperclips/tape) to avoid damage in transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred color-image source types
rubrics_metrics.description: For a color image (whether converted to black and white or to appear in color), submit one of the following (listed in order of preference): glossy color photograph; color transparency or interneg; color slide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide original high-quality color photographic media in the listed preference order to maximize fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-graphics print inclusion policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The AMS normally does not include color graphics in the print version of its journals, except in special circumstances. Color graphics that appear in black and white in print will appear in color in the electronic version as submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on color in print unless arranged with Editor/Publisher; color will be preserved in electronic publication if submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color-graphics resolution and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: When color graphics are warranted, color figures should have a resolution of at least 300 pixels per inch for photographic images and 600 pixels per inch for line art graphics when printed at 100%. Ideally they should be in EPS format; TIFF and JPEG are also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare color images at the specified ppi at final printed size. Prefer EPS (Encapsulated PostScript) for vector/line art; TIFF/JPEG acceptable for raster images. Note: PostScript is not the same as Encapsulated PostScript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed equations: linebreaking and width
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully, making sure they are broken and aligned following the guidelines in [Sw, pp. 38–41], and that they do not exceed the width of the page for the publication in which they are to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure displayed math fits within publication width and uses proper break/alignment conventions; consult AMS/Sw guidelines for linebreaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-line displayed equations
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-line displays, use the structures defined in the amsmath user's guide [ALG] or [Sp].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amsmath environments (split, align, multline, etc.) for multi-line equations rather than manual hacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial electronic submission location
rubrics_metrics.description: For AMS journals, see initial submission instructions on the Web at www.ams.org/peer-review-submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the AMS web instructions for initial electronic submissions; web submission is the primary route for peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial nonelectronic submission address
rubrics_metrics.description: Send one copy of the manuscript to: Centralized Manuscript Processing, 201 Charles Street, Providence, RI 02904-2294 USA. Clearly indicate the intended journal and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting hard copy, include journal name and contact info (email/postal) to avoid misrouting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only public CTAN macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 'public' macro packages (packages available from CTAN) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on private or nonstandard macro packages; use packages obtainable from CTAN to ensure processability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed other macro definitions in preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Other macro definitions must be embedded in the preamble of the article file. Electronic files must be able to be processed independently with all macros (not entire macro files) included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any custom macro definitions in the document preamble so the submission compiles standalone; do not expect production to load separate macro files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define macros with \newcommand (not \def)
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros should be defined with \newcommand, not with \def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \newcommand (LaTeX) or appropriate safe definition mechanisms to avoid accidental redefinition and to allow warnings when names already exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: No camera-ready submissions accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals do not accept camera-ready submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit finished camera-ready (production-ready) pages for journals; follow AMS production workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redeclare existing LaTeX/AMS commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeclare any existing LATEX, AMS-LATEX, or AMS-TEX commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redefinition of standard command names; use \newcommand or choose different names if conflict arises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperref policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The hyperref package will be added by Providence staff at the appropriate stage of the production process and will be applied to internal cross-references and external URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add hyperref yourself; production will apply it to ensure consistent behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use supplied template and document style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for your particular publication and the appropriate document style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start from the AMS author package/template for the targeted journal/series to ensure compliance with style and structure expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions. Page sizes must conform to the specifications for the journal for which you are preparing your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep default package/documentclass page geometry; do not hardcode margins or page dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No author-defined macros in top matter for electronic manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic manuscripts, do not use author-defined macros in author names, titles, abstracts, section headings, or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-matter fields should contain explicit text, not macros, so production tools and bibliographic services parse them correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: First page: descriptive title requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page of an article must contain a descriptive title. This title should be short, but informative; avoid useless or vague phrases such as 'some remarks about' or 'concerning'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a concise, informative title to aid reader understanding and bibliographic indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article title capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: In article titles, only the first word and proper nouns should be capitalized. Supply a shortened form of the title if the full title is too long for the running head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sentence-style capitalization for titles and provide a running-head short title when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid math in title
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the use of math in the title. Use of TeX math coding (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, rephrase to avoid inline math in the title; bibliographic services ingest titles literally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running heads formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The running heads on the left-hand (even-numbered) pages should have the name(s) of the author(s) in uppercase letters. Names in running heads should match the names as given on the first page. Shortened forms must be provided if necessary to fit on one line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide consistent author-name forms and any shortened versions for running heads to fit with page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS journal articles (except Book Reviews) must contain an abstract. The abstract should enable readers to take in the nature and results of the article quickly. The abstract should contain no text references to the bibliography unless the bibliographic reference is fully supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts may be multi-paragraph and include displayed material. Suggested upper limits: ~150 words for short papers, ~300 words for long papers. Avoid citations like '[3]' without full reference text in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide MSC codes (2010 scheme) for indexing; consult www.ams.org/msc/ for the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant and acknowledgments in top matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information on grants or contracts under which the research was performed, including grant number, using \thanks in an electronic manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include funding/contract acknowledgments in the indicated top-matter mechanism to ensure they appear correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-page footnotes: required and optional items
rubrics_metrics.description: Unmarked, unnumbered footnotes on the first page should include primary classiﬁcation numbers (required); grant information (optional); and key words and phrases describing the subject matter (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use first-page unmarked footnotes for MSC primary code (required) and optional grant/keywords; AMS style files automate formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliations and addresses placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other affiliations should appear at the end of your article, after the bibliography or references. A current address, if different from the affiliation, should follow the affiliation on a separate line. An email address should be included if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place affiliations as specified (endmatter for AMS); include current addresses and optionally emails. AMS style files handle formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography inclusion and BibTeX handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographic data must be incorporated into the article file. If you are using BibTeX, insert the contents of the .bbl file into your .tex file; do not send the .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed the processed bibliography (.bbl content) into the submitted .tex so production has full reference text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics margin and guidelines compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that any graphics do not extend into the margin; graphics must also conform to AMS graphics guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify figure widths and placement to avoid overlap into margins; follow the separate AMS Graphics guidelines document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your work before submitting it to the AMS. Author-prepared publications will not be given an editorial proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully check spelling, math, and formatting prior to submission; production expects submitted files to be proofed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to the author(s) when the accepted paper is received at the AMS; the signed form should be returned to the Production Department immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and return copyright/consent forms promptly. Authors retain certain reuse rights; see the form for options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs-specific requirements: chapter starts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page for Memoirs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Memoirs submissions, ensure chapter pagination follows right-hand page starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs-specific title capitalization and running heads
rubrics_metrics.description: In Memoirs chapter titles, the first and last words of the title and all nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbs should be capitalized; running heads: left-hand pages get chapter title uppercase, right-hand pages get section title uppercase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Memoirs capitalization conventions and provide shortened running-head forms as needed; AMS style files will apply uppercasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required software and versions for AMS-LATEX
rubrics_metrics.description: To use an author package, you will need: TEX and Computer Modern fonts; LATEX 2e (no earlier than June 1995) for AMS-LATEX; AMS-LATEX (amsart.cls, amsproc.cls, amsbook.cls); AMSFonts; and the appropriate publication-specific AMS-LATEX author package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you have current TeX/LaTeX and AMS packages installed; older versions may cause processing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS-TEX software requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If preparing a submission using AMS-TEX you need: TEX (including the plain format) and Computer Modern fonts; AMS-TEX (including amsppt.sty); AMSFonts; and the appropriate publication-specific AMS-TEX author package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install the listed AMS-TEX components if you choose AMS-TEX workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author package retrieval and installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain author packages from AMS web pages for monographs, proceedings, or journals; every author package is available bundled into a .zip ﬁle. Install style files in the directory where amsart.cls / amsppt.sty reside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrieve the correct package for your target publication; follow the Quick Start steps to install and test sample .tex files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AMS-provided structuring commands
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS style files contain commands to identify all the important features of mathematical papers and monographs; use these commands, not ones you define yourself. Quick reference lists of the most important structuring commands are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided section/theorem/exercise environments and predefined commands to ensure consistent structure and production compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Put frequent-expression definitions in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Put definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions together in the preamble section, before the start of the text of the manuscript. Once a macro is created for an expression, you should use it consistently for every occurrence of that expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define repeated macros centrally in the preamble to ensure consistent notation and easier maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid TeX coding for manual line/page breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use TeX coding to control line and page breaks; lines and pages may break differently in the published paper than in your file, and inserted break coding will have to be removed for production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let TeX handle pagination; avoid \vspace, manual pagebreaks, or explicit break commands unless instructed by production for camera-ready items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid explicit horizontal and vertical spacing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid explicit horizontal and vertical spacing commands for the same reason as manual breaks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert ad-hoc spacing to adjust layout; production may need to change layout and will remove these commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For camera-ready submissions only: check final output for line and page breaks; make sure that all text, equations, and graphics are within the margins. Submit your DVI and/or PostScript or PDF file(s) along with all related TEX and Encapsulated PostScript graphics files. The TEX file will be archived; the work will be printed directly from your output file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If producing camera-ready material (for some book series), produce and test the final output carefully and submit all files required to reproduce it exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitted source files must match accepted proof copy
rubrics_metrics.description: Before sending source files, be sure you have proofread carefully; the files you send must be the EXACT files used to generate the proof copy that was accepted for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send different or updated sources after acceptance unless instructed; ensure submitted files reproduce the accepted proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include printed copy or PDF matching submitted file
rubrics_metrics.description: For all publications, authors are required to send in a printed copy or PDF file of their paper that exactly matches the submitted file along with any graphics that will appear in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send a 'paper proof' (printed or PDF) that corresponds exactly to the submitted electronic files to help production verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundle multiple files into a single archive
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission consists of multiple files, bundle them using the Zip utility so only one compressed file needs to be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a zip bundle to reduce name conflicts and transfer errors; ensure all necessary files are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission methods and web account
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted electronic manuscripts can be submitted via the Web starting at www.ams.org/submit-book-journal. For security reasons, submitting through the web server requires an AMS Web Account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the AMS web submission as preferred method; create an account during submission if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Files sent by electronic mail should be addressed to pub-submit@ams.org and included as attachments, not as part of the message. The subject line should use the publication code to identify the book series or journal, and include author/editor names to speed processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach bundled files; set subject line to publication code and names for quick routing. Do not send DVI files inline or without appropriate encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTP submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Files can be transferred by FTP to ftp.ams.org into the 'incoming' directory; set mode to binary and use unique filenames. After transfer, notify pub-submit@ams.org with file name and publication information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow FTP protocol: login anonymous, cd incoming, binary mode, unique filename, then email production to report the transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical media submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Files can be sent on CD, diskette, or flash drive to the Acquisitions Department (books) or Production Department (journals). Label the media with name, paper title, and publication. Delete extraneous files and use protective packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label media descriptively, remove irrelevant files, package with stiffener/cardboard, and mark package as 'Electronic media. Do not fold or bend.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Textures users: extract DVI option
rubrics_metrics.description: If you created files using Textures, use the '.dvi' option from the 'save as' menu to extract the DVI file and include it in your submission bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure DVI is extracted correctly and included. For older Textures versions, use separate DVI tools if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding: use \newcommand (AMS-LATEX) or \define (AMS-TEX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use \def to define any command. With LATEX use \newcommand, and with AMS-TEX use \define.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the recommended macro-definition commands to receive warnings if a name already exists and to avoid accidental redefinition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard commands in section/theorem headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only standard commands in section or theorem headings; do not hard-code font changes or use commands that you have defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid explicit font directives in headings. Use the environments and styles provided by AMS-LATEX/AMS-TEX so production can handle them reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS theorem-style environment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the AMS-provided theorem styles (plain, definition, remark) and create theorem environments with \newtheorem in the preamble. Place all \newtheorem specifications in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify environments appropriately (Theorem/Lemma under plain, Definition/Problem under definition, Remark/Note under remark) and declare them in preamble to ensure correct numbering and formatting.
